candidate_name: Cardón IV / Perla field LNG export (Eni-Repsol)
sponsor_or_proposer: Eni SpA; Repsol SA (Cardón IV JV, operating the Perla field for PDVSA)
current_state: March-April 2026 strategic agreements between Eni, Repsol and Venezuelan authorities secure 2026 gas output and an export pathway from the offshore Perla field (Cardón IV block, ~17 tcf). Reporting (World Oil, 20 Apr 2026) frames LNG exports as a longer-term target 'by 2031', contingent on first reaching ~645 mmcf/d domestic supply AND further US sanctions easing. No LNG terminal location, no FLNG-vs-onshore decision, no FEED, no named terminal entity. The agreements are gas-production/export-pathway deals, not a concrete LNG-facility step.
missing_threshold_elements: concrete step (no LNG-facility FEED/site-selection/MOU for a terminal — agreement is upstream gas production); location (no LNG terminal site identified); arguably contingent (LNG export gated on sanctions relief + domestic-supply milestone)
watch_for: a named FLNG/onshore LNG terminal, a terminal site, a FEED award, or an LNG-specific MOU/FID for Cardón IV/Perla gas; sanctions changes that unblock export; any pivot from pipeline-to-Trinidad export toward a Venezuela-sited LNG facility
notes: Genuinely NOT in GEM (Eni/Repsol appear as owners of other countries' terminals only; no Venezuela Cardón/Perla terminal record). Distinct from the 4 dormant VE export terminals already in GEM (Delta Caribe Oriental/CIGMA, Project Venezuela LNG/Cristobal Colon, Sycar FLNG, Venezuela Offshore LNG/PDVSA-Rosneft). Eni entity not found in local GEM data under 'Eni SpA' (entity_lookup, local only — Eni does exist in GEM as a co-owner elsewhere, e.g. Congo FLNG, Darwin, Qatar North Field); a full entity check would re-run if this ever crosses the add threshold.
